title: eth_call execution gas capped at 2^24 after Amsterdam (EIP-8037)
body:
#### System information

Geth version: 1.17.7-unstable, commit `f8f9bc574459a1afefac7b63163739910ee0fe62` (master)
OS & Version: Linux amd64, Go 1.26.7

#### Expected behaviour

`eth_call` (and other simulations) given 50M gas, explicitly or through the default `--rpc.gascap`, can spend that gas on execution, as it can today on Osaka. Geth exempts `eth_call` from the EIP-7825 per-transaction cap (#32625).

#### Actual behaviour

With Amsterdam active, a call gets at most `2^24 - intrinsic_gas` of execution gas regardless of the gas requested. The rest goes to the EIP-8037 state-gas reservoir, which pure computation cannot use. A read-only call doing more than about 16.76M gas of computation fails with `out of gas`, with `gasUsed` exactly 16,777,216.

#### Steps to reproduce the behaviour

Start `geth --dev --http --override.amsterdam 0` (and, for comparison, `geth --dev --http` without the override). Then call, with state overrides so nothing needs deploying:

```sh
# Returns the gas left at the first opcode (code: GAS PUSH0 MSTORE PUSH1 0x20 PUSH0 RETURN)
curl -s -H 'content-type: application/json' localhost:8545 -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"eth_call","params":[{"to":"0x000000000000000000000000000000000000fe0f","gas":"0x2faf080"},"latest",{"0x000000000000000000000000000000000000fe0f":{"code":"0x5a5f5260205ff3"}}]}'
```

- without Amsterdam: `0x2fa9e76` = 49,978,998 = 50,000,000 - 21,000 - 2
- with Amsterdam: `0xffc566` = 16,762,214 = 2^24 - 15,000 - 2

A `pure` loop costing exactly 120 gas per iteration, with no state access and no memory growth:

```solidity
function burn(uint256 n) external pure returns (bytes32 h) {
    for (uint256 i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        assembly { mstore(0x00, h) mstore(0x20, i) h := keccak256(0x00, 0x40) }
    }
}
```

<details><summary>curl for burn(n) with the runtime bytecode as a state override</summary>

```sh

N=141487
curl -s -H 'content-type: application/json' localhost:8545 -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"eth_call","params":[{"to":"0x000000000000000000000000000000000000b0b0","input":"0x42966c68'$(printf '%064x' $N)'","gas":"0x2faf080"},"latest",{"0x000000000000000000000000000000000000b0b0":{"code":"'$BURNER'"}}]}'
```

</details>

`eth_call` over HTTP, default `--rpc.gascap` (50M), same results with `gas` = 50M and with no `gas` field:

| work (gasUsed on Osaka) | Osaka | Osaka + Amsterdam |
|---|---|---|
| ~10.0M | ok | ok |
| ~16.5M | ok | ok |
| ~17.0M | ok | `out of gas` |
| ~20.0M | ok | `out of gas` |
| ~40.0M | ok | `out of gas` |

`debug_traceCall` and `eth_simulateV1` with `validation: false` behave the same (17M and above fail with `out of gas`, gasUsed 16,777,216). The same results were obtained through `ethclient/simulated` and through a `geth --dev` node on a custom genesis with `amsterdamTime: 0` (and Bogota unset). Full harness: https://github.com/wighawag/rpc_eth_call_gas_limit/tree/main/eip8037-eth-call-cap.

#### Cause

`eth_call` builds the message with `SkipTransactionChecks: true` ([transaction_args.go#L517](https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/f8f9bc574459a1afefac7b63163739910ee0fe62/internal/ethapi/transaction_args.go#L517)) and goes through `core.ApplyMessage` ([api.go#L757-L790](https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/f8f9bc574459a1afefac7b63163739910ee0fe62/internal/ethapi/api.go#L757-L790), [api.go#L831](https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/f8f9bc574459a1afefac7b63163739910ee0fe62/internal/ethapi/api.go#L831), [state_transition.go#L367-L374](https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/f8f9bc574459a1afefac7b63163739910ee0fe62/core/state_transition.go#L367-L374)).

- `preCheck` honours `SkipTransactionChecks` for the Osaka cap ([state_transition.go#L561-L564](https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/f8f9bc574459a1afefac7b63163739910ee0fe62/core/state_transition.go#L561-L564)).
- `execute` then calls `initRuntimeGasBudget` ([L740](https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/f8f9bc574459a1afefac7b63163739910ee0fe62/core/state_transition.go#L740)), which under Amsterdam sets `gasLeft = min(params.MaxTxGas-intrinsicGas, evmGas)` and puts the remainder in the state-gas reservoir, without looking at `SkipTransactionChecks` ([L502-L507](https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/f8f9bc574459a1afefac7b63163739910ee0fe62/core/state_transition.go#L502-L507)).
- Execution costs never draw on the reservoir ([gascosts.go#L89](https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/f8f9bc574459a1afefac7b63163739910ee0fe62/core/vm/gascosts.go#L89), [#L112](https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/f8f9bc574459a1afefac7b63163739910ee0fe62/core/vm/gascosts.go#L112)).

#32625 settled this for Osaka: no cap for `eth_call`, `debug_traceCall` and non-strict `eth_simulateV1`, cap kept for `eth_estimateGas` and strict `eth_simulateV1`. Under Amsterdam that exemption no longer has any effect on execution gas, because the cap has moved from `preCheck` into the gas split.

#### Impact

Read-only contracts that compute a lot in a view, for example fully on-chain NFTs whose `tokenURI` renders an SVG, work today with the default 50M gas cap and will fail after the fork. The errors do not point at the cause: `eth_estimateGas` reports `gas required exceeds allowance (50000000)`, `eth_simulateV1` without a gas field says the limit "was capped by the RPC server's global gas cap", and `callTracer` shows `gas: 50000000` for the top frame.

#### Question

Should simulations (`eth_call`, `debug_traceCall`, `eth_simulateV1` in non-strict mode) run with the whole requested gas as execution gas when `SkipTransactionChecks` is set, as they do on Osaka? For example, `initRuntimeGasBudget` could skip the `MaxTxGas` split for such messages. If the cap is intended, it would help to document it and to make the errors above say so.

References: [EIP-8037](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8037), [#32625](upstream issues 32625), [params.MaxTxGas](https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/f8f9bc574459a1afefac7b63163739910ee0fe62/params/protocol_params.go#L31).
